rewrite.summary: Members of the FullsizeChevy forum shared various ways they discovered FSC, including through search engines like Google and Yahoo, other websites such as SportRucks.com and S10Forum, and recommendations from friends or fellow truck enthusiasts.

Members of the FullsizeChevy forum shared various ways they discovered FSC. Here are some common methods:
- **Search Engines**: 
  - Google (e.g., "Google, I was looking for instructions on how to level my truck, and found Luke's directions")
  - Yahoo (e.g., "well i chose yahoo. cause on my puter when i type something in wrong it sends me into yahoo database" by CahtasZ)
- **Other Websites**: 
  - SportRucks.com (e.g., "1badgmc saw me on Sportrucks.com and asked me to help the guys about a brazilian Silverado's lights... And now I'm here. Loving this place!")
  - S10Forum (e.g., "Found this place from http://www.s10forum.com/" by AGUILAR3)
- **Friends and Recommendations**: 
  - A friend or fellow member recommended the site (e.g., "my friend told me about it before i even had an fsc. This site basically made me go with a chevy, before that i was undecided on what i wanted" by CamaroGuy87132)

post_rewrites.rewritten_content: Please share how you discovered FSC. Your input will be very helpful. If your choice isn't listed in the poll, feel free to mention it here. Welcome to FSC!

I chose Yahoo because whenever I make a typo on my computer, it directs me there. Recently, I bought a 2005 GMC truck and was looking for a GMC forum. I can't remember exactly what I searched, but it led me to the site I was trying to find.
Consider adding "Silverado" to the poll. I discovered this site while searching for Silverado using Internet Explorer. Usually, I only use a search engine if no results are found.

Originally posted by navihawk: 
You should consider adding "other" as an option in the poll. I found this place while searching for Silverado on Internet Explorer, and MSN might have suggested it. Typically, I don't use a search engine unless no results are returned. Since "other" doesn't benefit me, that's why I asked you to post if the topic mismatched.

Originally posted by navihawk: Consider adding "Other" to the poll. I found this site while searching for Silverado using Internet Explorer. It might have been an MSN search engine. Generally, I use a search engine only when none are available, so in that case, it would fall under "Other search engine."
The search results Google produced were unparalleled.
I was a member of ChevyTruckWorld.com when another user recommended this site. Since switching, I've found it to be superior in terms of community camaraderie and server speed.
My friend recommended this site before I had an FSC, and it convinced me to choose Chevrolet. Previously, I was uncertain about my car selection.
The link Google provided was exceptional.
1badgmc contacted me through Sportrucks.com to assist with issues related to the lighting system on a Brazilian Silverado. I am now here to help, and I am enjoying being part of this community.
I was searching for instructions on how to level my truck and found Luke's guide, which I found very helpful. I've been following his advice ever since.

While searching for images of a 2-door Tahoe, I stumbled upon 2doortech.com, a dedicated forum for 2-door Tahoes. After browsing through about 20 posts, I noticed one member included the FSC address in a picture at the bottom. The site is excellent, though it focuses more on lifting than lowering.
I recently stumbled upon FSC while searching for information on repairing my truck, and I've been following along ever since.
I discovered this location through http://www.s10forum.com.

I discovered it while searching for an enthusiast forum to discuss buying a diesel or an Avalanche. Previously, I was a member of the S-Series forum when I owned a Jimmy. [http://s-series.org/](http://s-series.org/) It's a great resource for GM truck owners, and the community is friendly.
A few members from Exceeding Limits recommended I join this forum. Even a former member who recently left the group is still active here. It's been a great place to read and learn a lot.
Visit dieselplace.com for high-quality diesel parts and services.

Thank you, HD Stud.
